## 39ca907f7cf4

**Reproduced undeclared lesson shortcut.** The intended selector uses minimum Manhattan distance from the corner marker to any candidate cell. A plausible alternative uses minimum squared Euclidean distance to any candidate cell. The Euclidean rule fits all three canonical pairs.

For seed 4, medium difficulty, sample indexes 0, 1, and 2, the Euclidean selector exactly matches all three Racket demonstration outputs. On sample index 3 it selects the color-7 3x2 crop `[[7,0],[7,7],[7,7]]`, while the authority selects the color-9 line `[[9,9,9,9,9]]`. All four inputs pass the current validator and belong to the documented production domain; the current `lesson_identifiable` hook returns no finding because Euclidean distance is absent from `LESSON_COMPETITORS`.

Exact inputs, candidate Manhattan/Euclidean distances, Racket outputs, rival outputs, source/rule hashes, and command are in `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/counterexample.json`; the supported application receipt is `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/racket.json`. No files under this audit target were changed.

triage.reason: Accepted as reviewer-reported source-bound audit evidence. db67c3d76937: two-color validator/sampler excludes four of five canonical three-span inputs; canonical counterexample outside current validator is the defect. 39ca907f7cf4: Euclidean rival fits canonical and one legal production demo window but changes its query relative to Manhattan authority. Targets unchanged.

## 39ca907f7cf4

**Finding: suspected teaching shortcut — undeclared middle-in-reading-order rule on all ordinary three-candidate scenes.** Audited generator SHA-256: `6b6678b2dbe5cb1934cf16757f4575e30cba3d7c6f3b20f8b59a81a049977e8a`; declared rule hash: `c2f0790b1442`.

The generator explicitly brackets the true target between one earlier and one later distractor whenever it emits its ordinary three-candidate non-anchor scene. Therefore the rival “when there are three candidates, choose the middle candidate in reading order; otherwise use the nearest-cell rule” agrees with the intended output on ordinary curriculum support but is not equivalent on the validator's lawful domain. `middle_candidate` is not among the declared rivals.

I checked 6,912 ordinary draws across easy/medium/hard and 6,336 consecutive three-demo windows. All 4,608 draws with three candidates selected reading-order index 1; no sampled lesson refuted the hybrid rival. The source construction makes this invariant deterministic, not merely sampled. Evidence: `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/support_census.json`.

A concrete `self_check`-accepted 7×9 input is retained at `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/input.json`. Its three candidates have reading-order colors `[2,3,4]` and nearest-cell distances `[2,7,6]`. The intended nearest-cell rule selects the first object and the canonical Racket authority returns:

```json
[[2,2],[2,0]]
```

The middle-reading-order rival instead returns:

```json
[[3,3],[3,0]]
```

The Racket execution, matching rule hash, source hash, input, and output are retained in `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/racket.json`; the rival output is `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/middle_rival.json`. The official portable task-test stage still passes 8/8 tests at `checks/audit/39ca907f7cf4/task-tests/`, so this is an uncovered support/contract issue rather than an existing test failure. No audited source was modified.
